main_body: A tall wooden cabinet filled with a 3x4 grid of small drawers/compartments, framed in dark red-brown, with a short dark base/legs.
top_band: Rows 1-4: a pale tan band (about 3 rows) with a bright orange top edge and a dark red strip below it at rows 5-6. It sits at the very top and reads as a header or cornice panel, not a horizontal top surface seen from above. It is the same flat face-on look as the front below.
evidence: Down the middle column: orange edge (row 1), pale tan band (rows 2-4), dark red strip (rows 5-6), then the front face of the grid of drawers with a dark red frame down to row 28. The tan top band has the same texture and flat look as a face-on panel (a sign or header), with no foreshortened top surface and no lighter front-edge line. The drawers are painted flat: each is a tan face with a small yellow handle and a dark lower edge, with only a mild inset. The whole piece is drawn like an architectural elevation, with a thin cap, so it fails.

style.evidence: The red-brown frame and tan drawers use dark material-tone edges instead of black outlines, and the drawers have a few steps of light, mid and dark plus a yellow handle. But the 4 steps are fewer than the roughly 6 of the references, and the repeated identical drawers are mostly flat. The large red frame areas and the tan header band are flat fills with little grain or speckle. Density per tile is lower than the stall and well, which carry many varied details.
